articles.title: फोनिज उपत्यका समन्वय समितिद्वारा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठको योगदानबारे चर्चा
articles.summary:
ललितपुर । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) उपत्यका समन्वय समितिले फोनिजको २७औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसरमा नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघका संस्थापक अध्यक्ष सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठको पत्रकारिता क्षेत्रप्रतिको योगदानबारे अन्तरक्रिया तथा छलफल कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरेको छ ।

ललितपुर उद्योग वाणिज्य संघ, मंगलबजार, पाटनमा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले नेपाली पत्रकारिताको संस्थागत विकास, पत्रकारहरूको हकहितको संरक्षण तथा व्यावसायिक पत्रकारिताको आधार निर्माणमा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठले पुर्‍याएको योगदान ऐतिहासिक र प्रेरणादायी रहेको बताए।

वक्ताहरूले पत्रकारितालाई लोकतान्त्रिक मूल्य–मान्यता, अभिव्यक्ति स्वतन्त्रता तथा उत्तरदायी सञ्चार अभ्याससँग जोड्न श्रेष्ठले खेलेको भूमिकाको स्मरण गर्दै नयाँ पुस्ताका पत्रकारले उहाँको योगदानबाट प्रेरणा लिनुपर्ने धारणा व्यक्त गरे।

श्रेष्ठले वि.सं. २००८ सालमा उहाँको नेतृत्वमा नेपाल पत्रकार संघ गठन भएको थियो, जसलाई नेपालमा पत्रकारहरूको पहिलो संगठित पेशागत संस्था मानिन्छ। पत्रकारहरूलाई एउटै छातामुनि संगठित गर्ने, उनीहरूको पेशागत हक–हितको आवाज उठाउने तथा पत्रकारितालाई संस्थागत स्वरूप दिन उहाँले महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निर्वाह गर्नुभएको विभिन्न ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज र अनुसन्धानहरूले उल्लेख छ।

यद्यपि, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघको संस्थापक अध्यक्षको विषय लामो समयदेखि विवादमा छ। एक पक्षले सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठलाई नै संस्थापक अध्यक्ष मान्नुपर्ने तर्क गर्दै आएको छ भने नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघले भने पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री कृष्णप्रसाद भट्टराईलाई संस्थापक अध्यक्षका रूपमा लिएका छन् ।

यही विषयलाई लिएर फोनिजलगायत विभिन्न संघसंस्थाहरूले ऐतिहासिक तथ्य र दस्तावेजका आधारमा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठलाई आधिकारिक रूपमा संस्थापक अध्यक्ष घोषणा गर्न पटक–पटक माग गर्दै आएका छन्।

फोनिज उपत्यका समन्वय समितिले स्थापना दिवसलाई केवल औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा सीमित नराखी नेपाली पत्रकारिताका अग्रज व्यक्तित्वको योगदानबारे विमर्श गर्ने उद्देश्यले कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको जनाएको छ।

articles.title: लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफको प्रथम क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल एमडी ३२५ अन्तर्गत डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफ, नेपाल (लायन वर्ष २०२६–२०२७) को प्रथम डिष्ट्रिक्ट क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा क्याबिनेट अफिसर्स इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम आइतवार सम्पन्न भएको छ । डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नर लायन अजय प्रसाद खनालको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त क्याबिनेट मिटिङमा डिष्ट्रिक्ट भरिका लायन्स लिडरहरू, क्लब पदाधिकारी तथा सदस्यहरूको उत्साहजनक एवं उल्लेखनीय सहभागिता रहेको थियो । बैठकमा लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको मूल मन्त्र हामी सेवा गर्छौलाई आत्मसात गर्दै चालू लायन वर्षका रणनीतिक योजनाहरू, सेवा गतिविधि, नेतृत्व विकास तथा संगठन सुदृढीकरणका विषयमा गहन र रचनात्मक छलफल गरिएको थियो ।

विशेषगरी, लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको ग्लोबल कज अन्तर्गतका मुख्य क्षेत्रहरू मधुमेह, दृष्टि, भोक निवारण, पर्यावरण, बाल क्यान्सर, मानवीय कार्य, विपद् राहत र युवा जस्ता विश्वव्यापी प्राथमिकताका कार्यक्रमहरू लगायत डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नरका प्रायोरिटी प्रोजेक्ट तथा मानवीय सेवामूलक अभियानहरूलाई अझ प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढाउने, सदस्यता अभिवृद्धि गर्ने तथा क्लबहरूको सक्रियता र क्षमता विकास बढाउने विषयमा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयहरू समेत गरिएको छ ।

सोही अवसरमा उपस्थित विशिष्ट नेतृत्वको समुपस्थितिमा नयाँ क्याबिनेट टिमको औपचारिक इन्स्टलेसन (शपथ ग्रहण तथा पदस्थापना) सम्पन्न गरिएको थियो । नवगठित क्याबिनेट टिमले जिम्मेवारी ग्रहण गर्दै आगामी कार्यकालमा समाजमा प्रभावकारी सेवा तथा सबल नेतृत्व प्रदान गर्ने सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

यस कार्यक्रमलाई भक्तपुर दिबेश्वरी लायन्स क्लबले आतिथ्यता तथा व्यवस्थापकीय सहयोग प्रदान गरेको थियो । उक्त भव्य कार्यक्रमले सम्पूर्ण लायन्स सदस्यहरूमा सेवाभाव, आपसी एकता र समर्पणको भावना अभिवृद्धि गर्दै समाजसेवामा अझ सक्रिय, उर्जावान र प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढ्न ठूलो प्रेरणा दिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: अफवाह होइन सद्भावमा अग्रसरता, सामाजिक–राजनीतिक अगुवा सार्वजनिक आह्वानमा सक्रिय
articles.summary:
सुनसरी । सुनसरीमा दुई समुदायबीच भएको झडपपछि विभिन्न जिल्लामा फैलिएको तनावका बीच कोशी–मधेशका विभिन्न सहरमा सामाजिक सद्भाव र धार्मिक सहिष्णुताको सन्देश दिँदै बृहत् सद्भाव ¥याली आयोजना गरिदैछ । देशका विभिन्न स्थानमा निकालिएका यस्ता ¥यालीले सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम हुने ठानिएको छ ।

सुनसरीमा भएको घटनापछि मधेशका विभिन्न जिल्लामा देखिएको तनावका बीच सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम गर्ने उद्देश्यले बृहत् सद्भाव ¥याली निकालिएको छ । जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय धनुषाको अगुवाइमा आयोजित ¥याली जनकपुरधामस्थित रेल्वे स्टेशनबाट शुरु भइ नगरका विभिन्न मुख्य सडक हुँदै सम्पन्न भएको थियो ।

¥यालीमा राजनीतिक दलका प्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षा निकाय, स्थानीय तहका जनप्रतिनिधि, धार्मिक अगुवा, नागरिक समाज तथा उद्योगी–व्यवसायीहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

धनुषाका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी प्रेमप्रसाद लुइँटेलले मिथिला सभ्यता र संस्कृतिले सधैँ शान्ति, सहिष्णुता र सद्भावको सन्देश दिएको उल्लेख गर्दै सामाजिक एकता जोगाउन सबैलाई जिम्मेवार र संयमित बन्न आग्रह गरे ।

नेपाली कम्युनिष्ट पार्टीका केन्द्रीय सदस्य दीपक यादवले सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न सबै समुदाय एकजुट हुनुपर्ने बताउँदै सुनसरी र सिरहाका घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न माग गरे ।

जनकपुरधाम उपमहानगरपालिकाका पूर्वउपमेयर असगर अलीले घटनाबाट प्रभावितलाई न्याय दिलाउनुका साथै समाजमा विश्वास र सद्भाव कायम गर्न समुदायबीच निरन्तर संवाद आवश्यक रहेको बताए ।

यता, मोरङको लेटाङ नगरपालिकाका नगर प्रमुख भुपेन्द्र कुमार लावतीले २०६५ साल देखि नै लेटाङमा अन्तरधार्मिक शान्ति संजाल गठन गरेर सबै धर्म र जातजाति बीच सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम गर्राईरहेको जानकारी दिए ।

सामाजिक सञ्जालमा देखिने विभिन्न अफवाहलाई रोक्दै सद्भाव कायम गर्नुपर्ने गरि सार्वजनिक अपिल गर्न थालिएको छ। केहिदिनदेखि अशान्त बनेको तराई मधेसमा विस्तारै शान्ति स्थापनाका निम्ति नागरिक नै जागरुक बन्न थालेका छन्। यद्यपी वीरगञ्ज र सिरहाको गोलबजारलगायतका केही क्षेत्रमा भने निषेधाज्ञा अझै कायम रहेको प्रशासनले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीको तेस्रो उपन्यास ‘तेजस्’ सार्वजनिक
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । लेखक तथा अध्यापक शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीको तेस्रो उपन्यास ‘तेजस्’ सार्वजनिक भएको छ। शनिबार एक कार्यक्रमबीच बुद्धविहार काठमाडौँका भिक्षु कोण्डन्य, आख्यानकार एवं अनलाइनखबरका प्रधान सम्पादक बसन्त बस्नेत, संस्कृतिकर्मी नानी हेरा शाक्य, राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का नेता मिलन पाण्डे र कवि रुपक अलंकारलले पुस्तकको संयुक्त विमोचन गरेका हुन्।

कार्यक्रममा भिक्षु कोण्डन्यले ‘तेजस्’मा राणाकालमा बौद्ध समुदायमाथि भएको दमन र भिक्षुहरूलाई देशनिकाला गरिएको प्रसंग तथा पञ्चायतकालमा उनीहरू स्वदेश फर्किएको इतिहासलाई समेटिएको बताए।

उपन्यासले भाषा, संस्कार र संस्कृतिको संरक्षणको सशक्त सन्देश दिएको उनको भनाइ थियो। विपश्यना र बौद्ध दर्शनका पक्षहरू पनि कथामा प्रभावकारी रूपमा समेटिएको भन्दै उनले उपन्यास सशक्त र पठनीय भएको बताए ।

आख्यानकार एवं अनलाइनखबरका प्रधान सम्पादक बस्नेतले ‘तेजस्’ काठमाडौँको भूगोल र इतिहास बुझ्न अत्यन्त उपयोगी कृति भएको बताए।

सेतो ख्याकको दृष्टिकोणबाट कथा भनिएकाले उपन्यास रहस्यमय बनेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले बौद्ध धर्ममाथि राज्यले विभिन्न कालखण्डमा गरेको उपेक्षा र दमनलाई पुस्तकले गहिराइका साथ उजागर गरेको उनको भनाइ थियो। ‘कान्तिपुर (काठमाडौँ) को भूगोल र इतिहासको यो एउटा टुर गाइड पुस्तक बनेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘किताब स्वादको बनेको छ। संगठन नबनाइ एक्लै एक्लै काम गर्दा बिद्धस्टहरूलाई राज्यले कति सतायो भन्ने दस्तावेज हो यो किताब।

रास्वपा नेता पाण्डेले असन, वसन्तपुर, नेवार समुदाय र ख्याकसँग सम्बन्धित धेरै कम सुनिएका कथा पुस्तकमा समेटिएको उल्लेख गर्दै उपन्यासले काठमाडौँका सम्पदालाई हेर्ने आफ्नो दृष्टिकोण नै परिवर्तन गरेको बताए।

संस्कृतिविद् नानीहेरा शाक्यले उपन्यासले नेपाल मण्डलकालीन कान्तिपुर, वसन्तपुर, कुमारीघर र चित्लाङसम्मको परिवेशलाई जीवन्त रूपमा उतारेको बताइन्। नेवार समुदाय कसरी क्रमशः सीमान्तकृत भयो भन्ने विषयलाई संवेदनशील ढंगले प्रस्तुत गरिएको भन्दै उनले नेपाल भाषाका केही शब्दमा सामान्य त्रुटि रहेको पनि औंल्याइन्।

कवि रूपक अलंकारले अध्ययनशील लेखकका रूपमा अधिकारीको प्रशंसा गर्दै ‘तेजस्’ कुनै एक पात्रको कथा मात्र नभई समयसँगै बदलिएको काठमाडौँ, नेवारी संस्कृति र बौद्ध धर्मको रूपान्तरणको कथा भएको बताए। शाहकाल र त्यसपछिका राजनीतिक परिवर्तनले काठमाडौँ र बौद्ध परम्परामा पारेको प्रभावलाई उपन्यासले प्रभावशाली रूपमा चित्रण गरेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

लेखक शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीले उपन्यास लेख्ने क्रममा नेपालबाट बौद्ध भिक्षुहरू देशनिकाला गरिएको इतिहासले आफूलाई गहिरो रूपमा छोएको बताए। नेवारी समुदायको जीवन र संस्कृतिलाई नजिकबाट बुझ्न आफूले लामो समय अध्ययन र सहकार्य गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले इतिहास, मिथक र सामाजिक यथार्थलाई जोडेर ‘तेजस्’ तयार भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

शिखा बुक्सले प्रकाशन गरेको पुस्तकको मूल्य ७२५ रुपैयाँ तोकिएको छ।

articles.title: सद्भाव कायमम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायको आफ्नै योजना
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सुनसरीको देवानगन्जमा आइतबार भएको दुई समूहबीचको झडपपछि विग्रिएको परिस्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ । सुनसरीबाट मधेसका जिल्लातर्फ परेको बाछिटा पनि कम हुँदै गएको छ ।

स्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएपछि धनुषा, सिरहा, सुनसरी, सप्तरीमा र वीरगन्जमा लगाइएको कफ्र्यु हटाएर निषेधाज्ञा मात्र जारी गरिएको छ । विशेषगरी अहिले भइरहेको घटनामा सुरक्षा निकायको मूल्यांकन के छ ? अनि तनाव न्यूनीकरण र सद्भाव कायम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायले के गरिरहेको छ त ?

दुई समुदायबीच उत्पन्न तनाव मत्थर पार्न सुरक्षा निकायले विभिन्न रणनीति अपनाएको छ । त्यस मध्येको पहिलो रणनीति हो– उच्च अधिकारीहरूलाई फिल्डमा खटाउने । नेपाल प्रहरीले सुरक्षा व्यवस्था सुदृढ बनाउन ४ एआईजीसहित दुई दर्जनभन्दा बढी उच्च अधिकारीलाई कोशी र मधेश प्रदेशमा खटाएको छ । उनीहरूले त्यहाँको वस्तुस्थिति बुझेर केन्द्रमा रिपोर्ट पठाउने र त्यसैका आधारमा जनशक्ति खटाउने तयारी गरिएको छ ।

प्रहरीका उच्च अधिकारीहरु को कहाँ ?

प्रहरी अतिरिक्त महानिरीक्षक सिद्धिविक्रम शाहलाई बाँके, उमाप्रसाद चतुर्वेदीलाई कपिलवस्तु र ईश्वर कार्कीलाई सुनसरी पठाइएको छ । प्रहरी नायब महानिरीक्षक दिनेशकुमार आचार्यलाई सिरहा र अभिनारायण काफ्लेलाई सप्तरीमा खटाइएको छ ।

प्रहरी वरिष्ठ उपरीक्षक गोपालचन्द्र भट्टराईलाई सर्लाही, सोमेन्द्रसिंह राठौरलाई पर्सा, दीपशमशेर राणालाई रौतहट, नवराज अधिकारीलाई चितवन, कृष्णप्रसाद पंगेनीलाई महोत्तरी र होविन्द्र बोगटीलाई बारामा पठाइएको छ। त्यसैगरी, ज्ञानेन्द्रप्रसाद फुयाँललाई मोरङ, भुवनेश्वर तिवारीलाई धनुषा र अमरेन्द्रबहादुर सिंहलाई मधेस प्रदेशमा खटाइएको छ ।

उनीहरुले विकसित घटनाक्रमअनुसार सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने, जनशक्ति तथा स्रोतसाधन परिचालनको प्रभावकारिता मूल्यांकन गर्ने र आवश्यक नीति निर्देशन दिनेछन् । उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षा योजना कार्यान्वयन, सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणलगायत जिम्मेवारी पनि दिइएको छ।

सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष

लगातार बसेका सुरक्षा बैठकले सुनसरी घटनामा सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष निकालेका छन्। सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणमा सुरक्षा निकायले सन्तोषजनक काम गर्न नसकेको बैठकको निष्कर्ष छ । घटनालाई सामान्य रूपमा लिएर बेलैमा नियन्त्रणको प्रयास नगर्दा मानवीय तथा भौतिक क्षति बढेको पनि बैठकको विश्लेषण छ ।

यसैलाई मध्यनजर गरेर सुरक्षा निकायले सीमा क्षेत्रबाट आउने नयाँ व्यक्तिलाई निगरानीमा राखिएको छ । ड्रोनबाट हुने अनुगमनलाई पनि सक्रिय बनाइएको छ ।

दोस्रो सुरक्षा रणनीति हो–दुई पक्षलाई भेट हुन नदिने ।

सम्भावित जोखिम न्यूनीकरण गर्नका लागि तत्काल दुई पक्षलाई टाढै राख्ने गृह प्रशासनको तयारी छ ।

त्यसैगरी सुरक्षा निकायले बनाएको तेस्रो रणनीति हो– सुरक्षा फोर्सको तैनाथी ।

तनाव देखिएका कोशी र मधेशबाहेकका प्रदेशमा पनि अहिले सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई सतर्क अवस्थामा राखिएको छ ।

केही अप्ठ्यारो पर्ने अवस्था आएमा आवश्यक संख्यामा सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई तनाव देखिएका क्षेत्रमा पठाउने तयारी भइरहेको छ । तनाव न्यूनीकरणको चौंथो रणनीति हो– मठमन्दिर तथा मस्जिदहरू रहेका क्षेत्रमा अतिरिक्त सुरक्षा सतर्कता । फिल्डमा खटिन नपर्ने सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई धार्मिक स्थलहरूमा खटाइएको छ ।

अहिलेसम्म प्रहरीले साम्प्रदायिक÷सामाजिक सद्भावमा खलल पुरÞ्याएको भन्दै प्रहरीले ६५ जना व्यक्तिहरू पक्राउ गरेको छ । सिरहमा ५ जना, धनुषामा ४५ जना, सर्लाही ५ जना , महोतरीमा २ जना ,पर्सामा १ जना,सप्तरीमा १ जना ,सुनसरीमा २ जना ब्यक्तिहरु प्रहरीले प्रकाउ गरेको छ । सुरक्षा निकायले कुनै पनि किसिमका भ्रामक सामग्री सम्प्रेषण नगर्न तथा अनावश्यक उत्तेजित नहुन समेत भनेको छ ।

पाँचौँ सुरक्षा रणनीति हो– समन्वयको । प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीको संयोजकत्वमा जनप्रतिनिधि, धर्मगुरु तथा सुरक्षा निकायले छलफल र समन्वय गरिरहेका छन् ।साथै जनप्रतिनिधि र स्थानीय बासिन्दालाई गाउँ टोलमा नयाँ मान्छे आएमा सुरक्षा निकायलाई खबर गर्न पनि भनिएको छ ।

छैठौं सुरक्षा रणनीतिअनुसार सीमा नाकाबाट घुसपैठ हुनसक्ने परिस्थितिको जोखिम आकलन गर्दै त्यहाँ पनि सतर्कता अपनाइएको छ । सबै सुरक्षा रणनीति प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्न गृहसचिवको संयोजकत्वमा प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकसहितको कमान्ड फोर्सले एकीकृत सूचनासमेत संकलन गरिरहेको छ ।

सुनसरी घटनाबारे अनुसन्धान भइरहेकाले प्रतिवेदन नआएसम्म दोषी किटान गर्न नसकिने अवस्था रहेको सुरक्षा निकायको भनाइ छ ।

articles.title: निर्मल पुर्जासहित सबै आरोहीको निधन, कस्ता थिए कीर्तिमानी ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । कीर्तिमानी आरोही निर्मल पुर्जासहितका १० जनाकै निधन भएको छ। बिहीबारदेखि हराइरहेका पुर्जाको निधन भएको उनी संस्थापक रहेको संस्था एलिट एक्सपेडले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत पुष्टि गरेको छ। विश्वविख्यात पुर्जाको निधनले विश्वभर शोकको अवस्था बनेको छ ।

’आज, अत्यन्तै दुःख र मर्माहत हृदयका साथ हामी यो पुष्टि गर्दछौं कि ब्रोड पिकमा गएको हिमपहिरोमा परी निर्मल “निम्सदाइ“ पुर्जाले दुःखद रूपमा आफ्नो ज्यान गुमाउनुभएको छ। साथै, यस अभियानमा संलग्न अन्य सदस्यहरू पनि जीवित रहन नसकेको पुष्टि भएको छ।’ विश्व कीर्तिमानका लागि परिचित पुर्जासहित १० जनाले नै ज्यान गुमाएको घटनाले विश्वभर शोक मनाउन थालिएको छ।

१० जनाले नै गुमाए ज्यान

बिहीबार बिहान करिब ६ हजार ७ सय मिटरको उचाईमा पुगेपछि खसेको हिमपहिरोमा परी उनीहरु वेपत्ता भएका थिए। आरोहण दलको नेतृत्व गरेका पुर्जासहित विभिन्न देशमा आरोहीको खोजी तीब्र पारिएको थियो। हिमपहिरोमा परी ज्यान गुमाउनेहरुमा नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरूङ, किली पेम्बा शेर्पा ’किलु’, निमा शेर्पा र नवाङ थिन्डु शेर्पा, ओमानका नधिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी, अमेरिकी आरोही मालोरी गाइस, पाकिस्तानका सोहेल साखी र चीनका वाङ जोङ रहेका छन्। तीन जनाको शव शुक्रबार नै फेला परेको थियो भने पुर्जासहित अन्यको निधनको पुष्टी आजमात्रे भएको हो।

निर्मलको भावुक पोस्ट

निर्मल पुर्जाले ब्रोक पिक चढ्नुअघि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा लामो सन्देश लेखेका थिए। उनले ब्रोड पिक चढ्ने योजना नभएको समेत उल्लेख गरेका थिए। तर, उनले प्रार्थना गर्दै लेखेका थिए, ‘ब्रोड पिक– म तिमीसँग केवल एउटा कुरा माग्छु–मलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा माथि पुग्न र फेरि सुरक्षित रूपमा फर्किन देऊ ।’ यहि सन्देशमा उनले कुनै पनि हिमाललाई हल्का रुपमा नलिने जिकिर गरेका पुर्जा अब कहिल्यै नफर्किने गरि अस्थाएका छन्।

‘बेसक्याम्पबाट पहिलो पाइला चाल्नेबित्तिकै मेरो सम्पूर्ण समर्पण त्यही अभियानमा हुन्छ । सधैं त्यस्तै थियो । सधैं त्यस्तै रहनेछ,’ पुर्जाको अन्तिम सन्देश समेत यहि बन्न पुगेको छ ।

पुर्जाले सन् २०१९ मा विश्वका ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला सबै १४ हिमाल केवल ६ महिनाभन्दा केही बढी अवधिमा आरोहण गरेर विश्व कीर्तिमान कायम गरेका थिए । ८ हजार मिटर माथिका हिमाल आरोहण रेकर्ड हेर्दा यस पटक ब्रोड पिक चढेका भए चोयुबाहेक ८ हजार मिटर माथिका १४ वटै हिमाल विनाअक्सिजन दुई पटक आरोहण गर्ने विश्व कीर्तिमान उनको नाममा दर्ज हुने निश्चित थियो । अघिल्लो सातामात्र उनले पाकिस्तानको गसेरब्रम २ आरोहण गरी ५७औं आरोहण पूरा गरेका थिए । यस पटक ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको योजनामा भने नरहेको पनि उनले स्टाटसमा उल्लेख गरेका थिए ।

बेलायती सेनादेखि हिमालसम्म

म्याग्दीका निर्मल पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमै बेलायती सेनामा भर्ति भएका थिए। लामो समय बेलायतमै विताएका उनी बेलायती नागरिक समेत हुन्।पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमा सन् २००३ मा बेलायती सेनामा भर्ती भएका थिए । त्यसपछि सन् २००९ मा उनी रोयल मरिन्समा आबद्ध भए ।

उनले आफ्ना बुबा र दाजुहरूको बाटो पछ्याएका थिए । उनका बुबा र दाजुहरू सबै गोर्खा सैनिक थिए । गोर्खा सैनिकहरू नेपाली सैनिकहरूको प्रसिद्ध समूह हुन्, जसले २०० वर्षभन्दा बढी समयदेखि बेलायती सेनामा सेवा गर्दै आएका छन् ।

१६ वर्ष बेलायती सेनामा विताएका उनी पर्वतारोहणसम्बन्धि विशेष रुची राख्ने गर्थे। उनको असाधारण पर्वतारोहण उपलब्धिका लागि सन् २०१८ मा तत्कालीन बेलायती महारानी एलिजाबेथ द्वितीयले एमबीई (मेम्बर अफ द अर्डर अफ तजभ ब्रिटिस इम्पायर) सम्मान प्रदान गरेकी थिइन्। यो उत्कृष्ठ उपलब्धिका लागि प्रदान गरिने नागरिक सम्मान भएको बताइन्छ। उनी नेपाली मुलका बेलायती नागरिक भएपनि उनको निधनले नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्रीको श्रद्धाञ्जली

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाहले निर्मल पुर्जासहित ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको क्रममा ज्यान गुमाउनेप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गरेका छन्। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले लेखेका छन्, ’विश्वको १२औँ अग्लो हिमाल, पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वत–शृङ्खलामा अवस्थित ८,०५१ मिटर अग्लो ‘ब्रोड पिक’मा विश्व कीर्तिमानधारी निर्मल पुर्जा (निम्स दाइ) सहित छ जना नेपाली तथा अन्य चार विदेशी आरोहीहरूको दुःखद निधनले स्तब्ध बनाएको छ ।

निर्मल पुर्जा लगायत सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूको भौतिक यात्रा मात्रै रोकिएको हो, तर उहाँहरूको साहस, समर्पण र योगदानको इतिहास सधैँ प्रेरणायुक्त र जीवित रहिरहनेछ ।

सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जली ।’ उसोतः प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले हिमाल आरोहण शिखर चुम्ने यात्रा मात्रै नभई साहस, अनुशासन, त्याग र मानवीय सीमालाई चुनौती दिने अदम्य आत्मविश्वासको सर्वोच्च अभिव्यक्ति भन्दै हिमालले गौरव दिने तर, कहिलेकाँही आफ्नै काखमा सधैका लागि अंगालेर राख्ने बताएका छन्।

उनीहरुको समर्पणको इतिहास कहिल्यै नमर्ने भनेका शाहले शोक व्यक्त गरेका हुन्। उसोतः निर्मलसहितका आरोहीको निधनमा नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ भने विश्वभर नै यसको चर्चा र शोक व्यक्तको क्रम चलिरहेको छ।

articles.title: नेपालीलाई झन कडा ! २० हजार डलरको तगारो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित ५० देशका नागरिकले अब अमेरिकी बी–वान र बी–टु भिजिटर भिसाका लागि अधिकतम २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्ने भएको छ । अगस्ट ३ देखि लागू हुने नयाँ व्यवस्थाले भिसा आवेदन प्रक्रिया थप कडा र खर्चिलो बन्ने भएको छ ।

अमेरिका जाने योजना बनाइरहनुभएको छ ? विशेषगरी व्यापार वा घुमघामका लागि बी–वान वा बी–टु भिजिटर भिसा लिने सोचमा हुनुहुन्छ भने अब एउटा ठूलो परिवर्तनबारे तपाईल जान्नै पर्ने भएको छ । अमेरिकी सरकारले भिजिटर भिसामा लागू गर्दै आएको धरौटी प्रणालीलाई अब स्थायी बनाउने निर्णय गरेको छ ।

योसँगै धरौटी रकम पनि उल्लेख्य रूपमा बढाएको छ । अगस्ट ३, २०२६ अर्थात् पर्सी सोमवारदेखि लागू हुने नयाँ नियमअनुसार नेपालसहित तोकिएका ५० देशका बी–वान र बी–टु भिसा आवेदकले अब १० हजार, १५ हजार वा २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्नेछ । यसअघि परीक्षण कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत अधिकतम १५ हजार डलरसम्मको व्यवस्था थियो ।

सामान्यतया कन्सुलर अधिकारीले १५ हजार डलर धरौटी निर्धारण गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ । तर आवेदकको भ्रमणको उद्देश्य, रोजगारी, आम्दानी र अन्य अवस्थाका आधारमा यो रकम १० हजार वा २० हजार डलरसम्म हुन सक्छ । यो व्यवस्था पहिलो पटक अगस्ट २०२५ मा परीक्षणका रूपमा सुरु गरिएको थियो ।

अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार एक वर्षको अनुभवले यो प्रणालीले भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन प्रभावकारी भूमिका खेलेको देखिएको छ । यसो गर्दा उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको मन्त्रालयको भनाइ छ ।

भिसा प्रक्रिया कसरी शुरु हुन्छ ?

सबैभन्दा पहिले अन्य गैरआवासीय भिसा आवेदनजस्तै अन्तर्वार्ताको समय लिनुपर्नेछ र नियमित भिसा शुल्क तिर्नुपर्नेछ । त्यसपछि कन्सुलर अधिकारीले सबै योग्यता पुगेको र तपाईं तोकिएको देशको नागरिक भएको ठहर गरेमा भिसा तत्काल जारी हुँदैन । अध्यागमन तथा राष्ट्रियता ऐनको धारा २२१ जी अन्तर्गत भिसा अस्थायी रूपमा रोक्का गरिन्छ । त्यसपछि गृह सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयको धरौटी फाराम र सरकारी विद्युतीय भुक्तानी प्रणालीमार्फत धरौटी बुझाउन भनिन्छ । यो रकम आवेदक आफैंले वा तेस्रो पक्षले पनि तिर्न सक्नेछन् ।

धरौटी प्राप्त भएपछि अन्तिम समीक्षा हुनेछ । स्वीकृति पाए तीनदेखि १२ महिनासम्म वैध रहने सिंगल वा मल्टिपल इन्ट्री भिसा जारी हुन सक्नेछ । भिसामै धरौटी बुझाइएको विवरण पनि उल्लेख हुनेछ । अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार यो कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य रकम उठाउनु मात्रे होइन । एक वर्षको परीक्षणले यात्रुहरूलाई भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन यो प्रणाली प्रभावकारी देखिएको मन्त्रालयको निष्कर्ष छ ।

त्यस्तै उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको बताइएको छ । यद्यपि धरौटी फिर्ता हुने व्यवस्था पनि छ । त्यसका लागि भिसा बाहकले अनधिकृत रूपमा काम गर्नु हुँदैन, अनुमति अवधिभित्र अमेरिका छाड्नुपर्छ वा आवश्यक परे समयमै बसाइ अवधि थप अथवा भिसा स्टेटस परिवर्तनका लागि आवेदन दिनुपर्छ ।

सरकारी प्रणालीले सबै शर्त पालना भएको पुष्टि गरेपछि धरौटी स्वतः रद्द हुनेछ र पूरा रकम कुनै ब्याजबिना फिर्ता हुनेछ । तर यदि अनुमति अवधिभन्दा बढी अमेरिका बसियो, आवेदन ढिलो गरियो, अस्वीकृतिपछि १० दिनभित्र पनि अमेरिका छाडिएन वा शरण अथवा अन्य मानवीय संरक्षणका लागि आवेदन दिइयो भने धरौटी रकम स्वतः जफत हुन सक्छ । यस्तो अवस्थामा अन्तिम निर्णय भने होमल्याण्ड सेक्युरिटीले गर्नेछ । एउटा रोचक तथ्य के भने परीक्षण कार्यक्रम सुरु गर्दा एक वर्षमा करिब दुई हजार आवेदक मात्रै धरौटीको दायरामा पर्ने अनुमान गरिएको थियो ।

तर वास्तविक संख्या झन्डै २० हजार पुग्यो । तीमध्ये करिब आधाले मात्रै धरौटी बुझाए । त्यसको प्रभाव भिसा जारी हुने दरमै देखियो । कार्यक्रम लागू भएका देशका नागरिकका लागि बी–श्रेणी भिसा जारी हुने दर पहिलो १० महिनामै अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा ८३ प्रतिशतले घटेको अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ ।

यदि तपाईं अमेरिका भ्रमणको तयारीमा हुनुहुन्छ भने पक्कै पनि अब भिसा आवेदनको चेकलिस्टमा एउटा नयाँ कुरा धरौटी थपिएको छ । भिसाका लागि आवेदन दिनुअघि यो नयाँ व्यवस्था बुझ्न एकदमै महत्वपूर्ण छ । त्यसैले आवेदन अघि यी नियमहरू राम्रोसँग बुझेर मात्रै प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनु उपयुक्त हुनेछ ।

articles.title: मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द लोकतान्त्रिक एसोसियसन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मलेसिया रोजगारीमा एकाधिकार (सिण्डिकेट) लगाउन खोजिएको भन्दै वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संगठनहरूले आन्दोलनको चेतावनी दिएका छन् । नेपाल लोकतान्त्रिक वैदेशिक रोजगार एसोसियसनको आयोजनामा शुक्रबार काठमाडौंमा वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले यस्तो चेतावनी दिएका हुन् ।

एसोसियसनले मलेसिया रोजगारीमा केही व्यवसायीहरूले सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजेको भन्दै छलफल आयोजना गरेको महासचिव सुमनराज पाण्डेले बताए । ‘केही व्यवसायीहरूको निहित स्वार्थमा मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजिएको छ । यो विल्कुल गलत छ,’ महासचिव पाण्डेले भने, आजबाट सरोकारवालाहरूसँग छलफल शुरू भएको छ । सिण्डिकेट लागू भयो भने हामी आन्दोलनमा उत्रन्छौं । एसोसियसनले वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द पहल नगरे एक्लै भएपनि संघर्षमा उत्रने तयारी गरेको छ ।

छलफलमा एसोसियसनका पूर्वअध्यक्ष प्रज्ञान न्यौपाने, कुमुद खनाल, दीपक थापा, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघका निवर्तमान अध्यक्ष भुवनसिंह गुरूङ,संघका पूर्वमहासचिव मेघनाथ भुर्तेल, प्रगतिशिल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी मञ्चका उपाध्यक्ष सरिता घले, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायिक गणतान्त्रिक मञ्चका अध्यक्ष धनलाल जैशी, एकीकृत वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संगठनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष मीन प्रसाद गोलेसहित तामाङ समान, नेवा समाज, मगर समाज, महिला संघलगायत थुप्रै घटक संस्थाहरू सहभागी थिए ।

उनीहरूले व्यवसायीहरूको छाता संस्था वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघको भूमिकामाथि पनि प्रश्न उठाएका छन् । एसोसियसनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष सुवर्ण लामाले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द संघको ध्यानाकर्षण गराउने बताए ।

articles.title: स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति कौडीमा एनसेलले हात पारेपछि हंगामा, भुपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउपछि चासो बढ्यो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको सीआइबीले भण्डारीलाई अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरेको छ। भण्डारी किन पक्राउ परे? स्मार्ट प्रकरणमा भण्डारीको भूमिका के? चासो देखिन्छन्।

नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। स्मार्ट सेलको सम्पत्ति बेचेर राज्यलाई हानी नोक्सानी पु¥याएको आरोपमा उनी पक्राउ परेका हुन्। तत्कालीन समयमा रेखा शर्मा सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधिमन्त्री हुँदा भण्डारी विज्ञको रूपमा उनको सचिवालयमा नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

सचिवालयमा विज्ञ भनिएका भण्डारीलाई टेरामक्स प्रकरणले चिठ्ठा नै पर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। त्यसपछि टेरामक्स प्रकरणमा प्राधिकारणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनाल भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दाका कारण निलम्बित भएपछि उनले प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष पदमा सहजै पुग्ने स्थिति निर्माण गरे। तर, भण्डारी अध्यक्ष बनेपछि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा वेच्ने काम भएको बताइन्छ। राज्यको नाममा आईसकेको टेलिकमको सम्पत्तिलाई निजी कम्पनी एनसेललाई कौडीको भाउमा बेच्न सघाएको आरोपमा भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका हुन्।

के भन्यो सीआइबीले ?

नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)ले शुक्रबार ललितपुरको धापाखेलबाट पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ। उनलाई स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरिएको बताइएको छ। सीआईबीले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आएको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति बेइमानीपूर्वक सरकारको हक टुटाउन काम गराएको आरोपमा भण्डारी माथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको थियो।

दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० वैशाखमा अनुमति पाएको थियो। तर अनुमतिपत्र नवीकरण नगरेपछि स्मार्ट टेलिकमको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भएको थियो। यसरी सरकारको नाममा पुगिसकेको सम्पत्तिलाई बेचबिखन गर्नका निम्ति सघाएको आरोप भण्डारीमाथि समेत लागेको छ। प्राधिकरण नियामक निकाय समेत भएकाले पनि उनीमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने माग पहिलेदेखि नै उठ्दै आएको थियो । यता, ब्युरोले वैशाखमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमका तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध निर्देशक सर्वेश जोशीलाई पक्राउ गरिसकेको छ।

स्मार्टमा एनसेलको चलाखी

इजाजत खारेजीपछि विवादास्पद रूपमा सम्पत्ति लिलाम बिक्री भएको स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा निजी क्षेत्रको दूरसञ्चार सेवाप्रदायक कम्पनी एनसेल, त्यहाँका प्रमुख लगानीकर्ता र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वबीच शंकास्पद सम्बन्ध देखिएको भन्दै सीआइबीले अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ।

स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति बिक्रीबाट प्रमुख लाभग्राही एनसेल देखिएको छ। नेपाल दूरसञ्चार नियमावलीको नियम १० क मा एकै कम्पनीले एकभन्दा बढी दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकको अनुमति नपाउने उल्लेख छ। तर एनसेलमा लगानी गरेकाहरुले नै गैरकानुनीरूपले लिलामी गरिएको स्मार्ट टेलिकममा पनि लगानी सकारेकोे सीआईबीको ठहर छ ।

अहिले अनुसन्धानमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सेयर बिक्री, सेयर स्वामित्वको इतिहास, बैंक ऋण, सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न कारोबार हेरिएको छ। प्रहरीले स्मार्ट टेलिकम, त्यसका सेयरधनी, सम्पत्ति व्यवस्थापन, उपकरण बिक्री र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका आर्थिक सम्बन्धबारे अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रक्रियाभन्दा अगाडि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकम र एनसेलबीच सम्बन्ध देखिन्छ। यही आधारमा एनसेलसँग जोडिएका केही उच्च तहका व्यक्तिलाई पनि छानबिनको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ। स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रकरणमा एनसेलको नेपालस्थित सञ्चालकहरू सतिशलाल आचार्य, भावना सिंह श्रेष्ठ र सचिनलाल आचार्य पनि अनुसन्धानको राडारमै रहेका छन्।

दुरसञ्चार ऐन र स्वार्थको द्वन्द्ध

दुरसञ्चार ऐन २०५३ को दफा नंवर ३३ को उपदफा १ बमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले स्वामित्वमा आएको सम्पत्ति पूर्व अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिले उपदफा (३) बमोजिम निर्धारण गरिने मूल्य नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाई पुनः अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न सक्नेछ भनिएको छ ।

फेरि उपदफा २ बमोजिमको मूल्य निर्धारण गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि नेपाल सरकारले प्राधिकरणको परामर्श लिई बमोजिम विशेषज्ञ व्यक्तिहरुको एक समिति गठन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । तर, प्राधिकारणले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकम एनसेललाई बेच्ने कुरा नै असंगत, पदीय दुरुपयोग र भ्रष्टाचार हुने दाबीहरु सार्वजनिक भइरहेका छन्।

यस्तो अवस्थामा प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बनेका भण्डारीले पनि कानूनको उल्लङ्घन गर्दै स्मार्टको पक्षमा काम गरेकाले उनी अनुसन्धानमा तानिएका हुन्। तत्कालीन माओवादी केन्द्रबाट सञ्चारमन्त्री बनेकी शर्माले अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेका भण्डारीमाथि पदीय दुरुपयोगको गम्भीर आरोप लाग्दै गर्दा नियुक्ति दिने शर्मामाथि समेत केहिले प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। कतै यो सबै सेटिङमै त भएन?

प्रहरीले अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने बाटो यसतर्फ समेत केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिन थालिएको छ। यद्यपी शर्मामाथि यस्ता आरोप भने सार्वजनिक रुपमा लागेको देखिन्न। तर, सचिवालयको विज्ञ भनिएको कर्मचारीलाई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेपछि कानून मिचेको देखिदा उनीमाथि समेत यस्तो प्रश्न स्वभाविक बन्न पुगेको छ ।

articles.title: ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप नेपाल प्रवेश : जेम होम कलेक्सन आधिकारिक वितरक नियुक्त
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं। भारतको अग्रणी होम टेक्सटाइल कम्पनी ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गरेको छ। कम्पनीले नेपालका लागि आफ्ना होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको एकमात्र आधिकारिक वितरकको रूपमा जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेडलाई नियुक्त गरेको घोषणा गरेको छ। यस सहकार्यसँगै नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अब ट्राइडेन्टका प्रिमियम बेड लिनेन, बाथ लिनेन, तौलियालगायतका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू आधिकारिक तथा भरपर्दो माध्यमबाट प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्।

यसअघि नेपाली बजारमा ट्राइडेन्टका उत्पादनहरू प्रायः अनौपचारिक माध्यमबाट भित्रिने गरेकोमा यस नियुक्तिपछि गुणस्तर र प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितता हुने कम्पनीहरूको दाबी छ। यस साझेदारीले नेपालमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रियस्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको पहुँच विस्तार गर्ने र नेपाली ग्राहकहरूलाई विश्वस्तरीय गुणस्तर, आधिकारिक आपूर्ति शृंखला तथा उत्कृष्ट ग्राहक सेवा उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेड विगत ३० वर्षदेखि नेपालको फ्लोरिङ तथा फर्निसिङ क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय रहेको कम्पनी हो। यसले आतिथ्य र खुद्रा दुवै बजारका लागि विविध गुणस्तरीय उत्पादनहरू निरन्तर आपूर्ति गर्दै आएको छ। यही दीर्घकालीन बजार अनुभव र स्थापित वितरण सञ्जालका कारण कम्पनीलाई ट्राइडेन्टको आधिकारिक साझेदारका रूपमा छनोट गरिएको बताइएको छ।

ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपको स्थापना सन् १९९० मा भारतीय उद्यमी पद्मश्री राजिन्दर गुप्ताले पञ्जाबबाट सुरु गरेका थिए। सुरुमा एउटा मात्र धागो उत्पादन एकाइबाट सुरु भएको यो समूह हाल विश्वकै सबैभन्दा ठूला टेरी तौलिया उत्पादक र समग्र होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादकहरूमध्ये एक बनेको आर्थिक हिसाबले हेर्ने हो भने पछिल्लो प्रतिवेदन अनुसार ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२६ मा ६५ अर्ब २१ करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ बराबरको आम्दानी हासिल गरेको थियो, जुन अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा सामान्य घटेको भए पनि खुद नाफा भने बढेको थियो।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको हालसालैको प्रगति हेर्दा पनि, पहिलो त्रैमासमा आम्दानी १ हजार ८ सय ३० करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको र खुद नाफा ५५ प्रतिशतले वृद्धि भएको देखिन्छ। कम्पनीको समग्र आकारका सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा, ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप इन्डियामा हाल १६ हजार ३ सय तीनजना कर्मचारी कार्यरत रहेका छन् र यसको बजार पूँजीकरण करिब १।३२ बिलियन डलर बराबर रहेको पाइन्छ। समूह लामो समयदेखि आफूलाई एक बिलियन डलरभन्दा बढी मूल्यको वैश्विक व्यापारिक समूहको रूपमा चिनाउँदै आएको छ, जसको होम टेक्सटाइल, कागज र रसायन क्षेत्रमा सशक्त उपस्थिति रहेको दाबी गरिन्छ।

यसआधिकारिक वितरण सम्झौतापछि नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितताका साथ प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन् भने होटल तथा रिसोर्ट जस्ता आतिथ्य व्यवसायहरूले पनि विश्वसनीय आपूर्ति स्रोत भेट्टाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। साथै यसले नेपालको होम फर्निसिङ बजारमा स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा र गुणस्तर सुधारमा समेत योगदान पुर्‍याउने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

articles.title: मेची राजमार्ग ठप्प ! सडक बन्द हुँदा बिरामीदेखि ढुवानीसम्म संकट
articles.summary:
इलाम । मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलाम माइखोला राजदुवालीकमाथि सडक अवरुद्ध भएको तीन सात भयो । सडक खुल्ने अझै छाँटकाँट छैन । सडक बन्द भएपछि इलाम मात्र हैन पुर्वी पहाडी जिल्ला पाँचथर ताप्लेजुङ लगायतका स्थानीयलाई समेत सास्ती भएको छ ।

मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलामको माइखोला (राजदुवाली) माथिको सडक भासिएर तीन सातादेखि अवरुद्ध हुँदा इलामसँगै पाँचथर र ताप्लेजुङका नागरिकले सास्ती भोगिरहेका छन् । सडक बन्द भएपछि सवारी साधन वारिपारि नै रोकिने गरेका छन् भने यात्रुहरू करिब एक किलोमिटर भिरको बाटो पैदल हिँड्न बाध्य छन् ।

बिरामीलाई जनपथ प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाले स्टे«चरमार्फत वारपार गराइरहेका छन् भने एम्बुलेन्स पनि दुवैतर्फबाट सेवा दिन बाध्य छन् । अत्यावश्यक खाद्यान्न, ग्यास र तरकारी ढुवानीसमेत प्रभावित बनेको छ । इलाम नगरपालिकाले सरोकारवाला निकायसँग छलफल गरी पुनः इलामलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ ।

राजदुवाली खण्डको पहिरो नियन्त्रण, ट्रस्ट पुल मर्मत तथा जोरकलश–हर्कटे सडक स्तरोन्नतिको लागि २४ करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको ठेक्का जे एन्ड जे निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले २०८४ असारसम्म सम्पन्न गर्ने गरी लिएको भएपनि हालसम्म समग्रमा १८–२० प्रतिशत मात्र काम भएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयले जनाएको छ । स्थानीयले मुख्य सडकभन्दा वैकल्पिक सडक तत्काल सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन माग गरेका छन् ।

गत वर्ष तीन महिनासम्म संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गरिए पनि प्रभावकारी काम नभएको भन्दै स्थानीय आक्रोशित छन् । सरकारले सडक बनाउन नसके इलामेली आफैंले श्रमदान र चन्दा उठाएर सडक तथा पुल निर्माण गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

सडक अवरुद्धकै कारण बिरामीले समयमै उपचार नपाएर ज्यान गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको भन्दै तत्काल समाधानको माग गरिएको छ ।

उता वैकल्पिक सडकका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिने सिमलगोलाई–तिल्केनी तथा केचना–कञ्चनजंघा सडकको बेलासी–भन्ज्याङ खण्ड पनि निर्माणमा ढिलाइका कारण सञ्चालन योग्य छैन । माइजोगमाई र पुवा खोलाका पुल गत वर्षको बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिलेसम्म पुनर्निर्माण हुन सकेको छैन । यस वर्ष बजेटमै इलामलाई बेवास्ता गरिएको भन्दै स्थानीयले सरकारसँग तत्काल सडक सञ्चालनको सुनिश्चितता गर्न माग गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: Communal unrest exposes failures in Nepal’s intelligence system
articles.summary:
When communal tensions flared up in Dewanganj of Sunsari and swiftly spread across neighbouring districts in Madhesh province, Prime Minister Balendra Shah summoned Inspector General of Nepal Police Dan Bahadur Karki and Armed Police Force chief Narayan Datta Paudel to his office for an emergency briefing.

During the separate high-level consultations held at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers on July 29, Shah notably excluded Tekendra Karki, head of the National Investigation Department (NID)—the country’s sole civilian intelligence agency operating directly under his office.

During the meeting with the two security chiefs, Prime Minister Shah sought answers regarding the breakdown of order in Madhesh. “How did the situation in Sunsari go out of control? Under what exact circumstances were live rounds fired, and how did warning shots result in a civilian fatality?” Shah asked. A second victim succumbed to injuries the following day, July 30.

According to the briefings submitted by the two security chiefs, the initial confrontation erupted between two local groups in Sunsari at approximately 10:13 pm on July 26. A small police unit led by Assistant Sub-Inspector Prakash Kumar Shrestha from the Kaptanganj Police Post was dispatched to the scene.

As the crowd grew increasingly hostile, Shrestha requested urgent reinforcements. Inspector Rakesh Rai arrived shortly after from the Area Police Office in Dewanganj with an eight-man team. However, both security details were ambushed by violent mobs armed with wooden logs, stones, and bamboo sticks, forcing an immediate retreat.

Under heavy assault, Inspector Rai fired three warning rounds from his pistol. The security heads stated that a subsequent Armed Police Force unit deployed to regain control of the perimeter fired at least 20 warning shots at around 10:45 pm.

A former chief investigation director of the NID said Prime Minister Shah missed a critical independent perspective by omitting the intelligence chief from these briefings.

“In Siraha, it remains completely unverified who actually fired the lethal bullet, as neither security agency has admitted that their personnel fired the fatal round,” he said. “Had the prime minister consulted the NID chief, he could have received objective, unvarnished information distinct from the operational accounts offered by the frontline police forces.”

However, Prime Minister Shah saw little utility in meeting NID chief Karki. By statutory mandate, the department is charged with gathering preemptive intelligence on matters threatening national security and alerting the executive before crises erupt. While law enforcement agencies act after the fact, the NID is expected to operate beforehand.

According to its official mandate, the department’s core responsibilities encompass collecting intelligence on economic crimes, terrorism, and organised crime, as well as detecting threats to religious, cultural, and communal harmony.

Yet, the NID has repeatedly stumbled in its core mission and led political leaders to systematically discount its strategic assessments. This systemic disuse peaked during the Gen Z protests on September 8 last year, when then-prime minister KP Sharma Oli reportedly left an entire week of intelligence dossiers unread on his desk.

In the latest Sunsari tension, the intelligence structure failed to deliver any advance warning of widespread communal unrest. Home Minister Sudan Gurung recently confirmed that no state agency provided actionable intelligence ahead of the clash in Sunsari.

Operationally, the NID had deployed a team in Sunsari led by Deputy Investigation Director Bimal Ghimire, supported by a provincial intelligence structure headed by Investigation Director Indra Lama. Yet, this entire network failed to detect the rising communal tension.

“This is hardly the first instance where our premier intelligence agency failed to provide advance warning on critical national security developments,” a senior official at the Prime Minister’s Office revealed. “In several previous instances, when the prime minister requested specific briefings, the department leadership was entirely oblivious to the situation on the ground.”

A deputy investigation director within the department expressed dismay that while the chief district officer and law enforcement leadership in Sunsari were summarily replaced following the clashes, the NID setup remained entirely untouched.

“The situation has reached a point where political authorities seem to have forgotten that an intelligence agency even exists,” the official lamented. “In Sunsari, the failure was not limited to the police and armed forces; the civilian intelligence apparatus failed completely.”

Ironically, Prime Minister Shah had reshuffled the Business Allocation Rules on May 15 specifically to strengthen the NID by pulling it directly under the purview of the Prime Minister’s Office.

According to an official at the department, former secretary Govinda Bahadur Karki, currently serving as the chief secretary, had received routine reports from the NID and advocated bringing the agency directly under the prime minister to build a robust information-gathering body.

Former prime minister Oli had similarly centralised the agency under his office prior to the Gen Z movement and drew sharp political criticism for consolidating state power.

The election government led by Sushila Karki subsequently returned the NID to the Ministry of Home Affairs. However, the Good Governance Roadmap 2025 explicitly recommended ending the practice of shifting the agency between ministries, advocating for its permanent placement under the Prime Minister’s Office to ensure institutional stability.

Although the agency returned under Prime Minister Shah’s office, it failed to earn the executive’s operational confidence.

In the past, the agency was brought under the Prime Minister’s Office with the intent of developing counter-intelligence capabilities. Intelligence officers anticipated enhanced political backing to modernise the organisation. Instead, despite operating under a strong government, the department faced unprecedented neglect.

“The NID’s budget has been drastically slashed this fiscal year, with operational funds for information gathering cut by 50 percent,” said a senior official at the department. “Field intelligence requires sustained financial investment. When field officers lack basic resources, intelligence gathering collapses.”

While overall budgetary allocations for home administration were scaled down by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in the latest budget, defense allocations saw a notable increase.

Commenting on the intelligence lapse, Nepal Police former additional inspector general Tek Prasad Rai, who served extensively in the Police Special Bureau, emphasised that Sunsari’s history of Hindu-Muslim friction required perpetual high-level surveillance.

“Several active local organisations in the area require continuous monitoring, yet our intelligence apparatus appeared completely oblivious,” said Rai. “This was a collective failure of both the NID and the specialised intelligence units of the Nepal Police.”

Rai highlighted that the Madhesh region had witnessed recurring friction over the hoisting of religious flags at Ramananda Chowk [Janakpur] and provocative public statements. “Even when the decision was taken to remove the disputed flag that triggered the violence, no proactive mediation was initiated. This represents a severe operational lapse,” he added.

Established in 1951 as the central intelligence department, the agency underwent multiple structural transformations. During the 1970s, the NID played a decisive role in gathering actionable intelligence on Khampa insurgents operating in Mustang, earning widespread praise for enabling security forces to disarm the rebellion.

“NID officers provided precise intelligence to security forces showing that arms were being smuggled from Pokhara under the guise of Red Cross humanitarian aid,” said Rajendra Kunwar, author of books detailing the Khampa insurgency.

On August 12, 1975, NID intelligence led to the arrest of a foreign embassy official in possession of confidential cabinet minutes, a case that implicated Bijay Chapagai, private secretary to then Assistant Minister for Water Resources Dhyan Bahadur Rai. During the height of the Maoist conflict after 1996, the department conducted 'Operation Mustang' in coordination with Britain's MI6.

However, following the political change of 1990, the agency’s external intelligence functions were stripped, restricting its scope strictly to domestic intelligence. Department veterans lament that after 1993, successive political administrations reduced the agency to a patronage hub for political appointments.

Former home ministers, including Govinda Raj Joshi, Khum Bahadur Khadka, and Bamdev Gautam, faced persistent criticism for filling department positions with political loyalists. Consequently, the NID’s core function degraded into compiling press clippings and preparing routine political dossiers.

Addressing these structural flaws, former NID additional chief investigation director Shreepurush Dhakal remarked that while discussions frequently reference global agencies like the CIA (USA), RAW (India), or Mossad (Israel), commentators overlook the strategic priority that foreign leaders accord to intelligence.

“The NID often submits intelligence reports, but when decision-makers fail to review or act upon them, organisational capacity naturally erodes,” Dhakal told Kantipur. “Strengthening the NID requires firm political will, followed by targeted financial investment and capacity building. When the state leadership takes intelligence seriously, these operational failures will disappear.”

articles.title: Shah to resume stalled one-on-one meetings with selected ambassadors next week
articles.summary:
Breaking his self-imposed rule, Prime Minister Balendra Shah last week planned one-on-one meetings with ambassadors from selected countries.

Accordingly, informal communication was sent to Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava, Chinese Ambassador Zhang Maoming, and the US Embassy’s Chargé d’Affaires Scott Urbom.

After receiving communication that they would be contacted for meetings with the prime minister, the ambassadors expressed their happiness about the prospect, according to officials at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and staff members of the respective embassies.

“We could easily sense a kind of excitement among the ambassadors after they were informed about meeting the prime minister. Personally, they had sent private messages to the divisional heads at the foreign ministry and others about the preparation,” said an official at the ministry.

However, the prime minister’s plan has yet to materialise. His aides attributed the delay to the communal tensions in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

“The initial plan to meet the Indian and Chinese ambassadors separately has not changed,” said one of Shah’s aides. “While the exact dates have yet to be announced, the meetings, being coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, are expected to take place next week.”

Shah had been maintaining a self-imposed rule of not holding one-on-one meetings with Kathmandu-based ambassadors, which led him to hold a meeting in a group. His move to hold joint meetings with Kathmandu-based ambassadors on April 9 and May 26 was widely praised by Nepali diplomats, foreign policy experts and observers as a more transparent and equitable approach to diplomatic engagement.

However, after the government completed 100 days in office, political adviser Asim Shah and others advised the prime minister to begin meeting with various domestic stakeholders, including members of the business community, media representatives, contractors, and Kathmandu-based ambassadors, according to priority.

His consultations with business communities and his decision to move away from his earlier stance of not holding individual meetings with ambassadors were the result of recommendations from his advisers, according to the aide.

“It is only natural to begin with the ambassadors of our two neighbours, India and China, given Nepal’s foreign policy priorities,” said the aide.

To underscore that New Delhi and Beijing are equally important to Nepal, Shah is scheduled to meet Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava and Chinese Ambassador Zhang Maoming on the same day, followed by a meeting with the US Embassy’s Chargé d’Affaires.

Shah, who assumed office as prime minister on March 27, had initially refused to meet even senior US diplomats visiting Nepal. He turned down requests from the US Embassy in Kathmandu for meetings with US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Samir Paul Kapur and President Donald Trump’s special envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gor.

US Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers also did not receive an audience with the prime minister during her visit.

In the past, newly elected prime ministers would meet foreign ambassadors individually at the Prime Minister’s Office or their official residence within days of assuming office.

articles.title: Northern border disruptions and higher duties slow Nepal’s EV boom
articles.summary:
Months-long disruptions at Nepal’s two main northern border crossings have slowed the country’s fast-growing electric vehicle (EV) market, caused imports to fall sharply, and threatened the launch of new models ahead of this month’s two biggest automobile exhibitions.

EV imports, which had expanded rapidly over the past five years and made Nepal one of the world’s fastest adopters of electric mobility, dropped by 24.03 percent in the last fiscal year ended mid-July, according to the Department of Customs.

Overall imports of four-wheelers—including passenger buses, microbuses and private vehicles—declined by 19.07 percent during the review period.

Nepal imported 17,688 four-wheelers worth Rs40.44 billion in the last fiscal year, of which 13,004 units were EVs valued at Rs31.32 billion.

The supply crunch comes as disruptions continue along the China border, raising concerns that automakers may not be able to unveil new models on schedule at the NAIMA Nepal Mobility Expo 2026, which begins on August 11, and the NADA Auto Show 2026, starting on August 25.

“We couldn’t import 400 to 500 EVs as planned in the last fiscal year because of disruptions at the China border,” said Yamuna Shrestha, managing director of Cimex Inc, the authorised distributor of Chinese EV leader BYD.

Trade through Nepal’s northern gateways has been repeatedly disrupted over the past year.

On July 8 last year, a flash flood in the Lhende river swept away the Friendship Bridge at Kerung, one of Nepal’s principal trade gateways with China. It took nearly six months for China to construct a temporary bridge. Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi customs point lies about 24 kilometres south of Kerung.

The Tatopani border crossing in Sindhupalchok was also shut for nearly three months last year after massive landslides blocked the route.

“The northern border points remained disrupted for four to five months in the last fiscal year, including the festive season. That itself was a huge loss for traders,” Shrestha said. “Although we managed to reroute some EV shipments through the Korala border point, importing from there was difficult.”

She urged the government to act more swiftly whenever trade routes are disrupted.

“The government should ensure smooth trade whenever such obstructions occur. This is not only about importing EVs but all goods. Major trade routes should be prioritised because we have not been able to deliver EVs on time as committed,” she said.

Dhruba Thapa, chairman of Himalayan Motrox, the authorised distributor of premium EV brand Maxus, said the decline in imports was also influenced by heavy stockpiling before the previous fiscal year’s budget.

“Most EV dealers imported 20 to 25 percent more vehicles than usual before the previous fiscal year’s budget because of rumours that duties on EVs would increase. That covered demand for four to five months, resulting in a slight drop in imports in the last fiscal year,” Thapa said.

“The prolonged closure of the Rasuwagadhi and Tatopani border points also made it difficult to introduce new models during the last Dashain and Tihar festive season,” he added.

According to traders, supply disruptions prevented dealers from delivering newly launched models displayed during last year’s Nepal Automobile Importers and Manufacturers Association (NAIMA) and Nepal Automobile Dealers’ Association (NADA) auto shows.

They warn that if the Tatopani crossing remains closed, this year’s exhibitions could face similar setbacks.

“I want to launch a new Maxus model at the auto show, but it is stranded at Tatopani because of landslides,” Thapa said. “Diverting the shipment through Kerung would create documentation and transportation hassles while increasing both time and cost.“

“Even if we try to reroute vehicles through the Korala border point, the distance from the Maxus factory to that border is too long, making it impractical,” he said.

According to Thapa, 12 to 13 Maxus EVs have been stranded at Tatopani for more than two weeks.

Shyam Sapkota, president of the Electric Vehicle Importers and Manufacturers Association of Nepal, said members also plan to introduce new models during the auto shows, but many vehicles remain stranded at the border.

Himalayan Motrox imported 30 Maxus EVs last year and sold around 25 units during the year.

Thapa said demand for luxury EVs had been rising until the last fiscal year, but higher import duties introduced in the current fiscal year’s budget have sharply increased prices and rendered premium models less affordable.

The price of the Maxus MIFA 7, for example, has jumped from Rs10.25 million to Rs20.45 million in the current fiscal year.

The company is now targeting sales of around 100 Maxus electric pickup trucks this fiscal year. A Maxus pickup is priced at Rs8.8 million.

Chinese brands continued to dominate Nepal’s EV market. Of the Rs31.32 billion spent on EV imports last fiscal year, Rs23.55 billion went to Chinese models. India accounted for Rs5.22 billion, while imports from Thailand, the UK, Germany, South Korea, the United States and Austria totalled Rs2.60 billion.

Nepal imported 9,640 EVs from China, 2,507 from India and 860 from other countries.

“Road conditions on the Tatopani route are poor, while customs clearance at Rasuwagadhi takes considerable time. Documentation procedures have become stricter since the beginning of the current fiscal year,” Sapkota said.

He said around 60 EV brands—including electric cars, jeeps, vans and microbuses—are now available in Nepal.

“With so many brands in the market, competition has become intense, and customers are also becoming confused by the wide range of choices,” Sapkota said.

Despite logistical challenges, dealers say consumer demand for EVs remains strong.

However, following the new tax regime, buyers who previously looked for vehicles priced between Rs4 million and Rs5 million are shifting to models costing less than Rs4 million. Demand for premium EVs priced above Rs5 million has weakened, while competition in the lower-priced segment has intensified.

According to the National Transportation Policy 2026 prepared by the Ministry of Infrastructure Development, Nepal had registered 63,280 EVs by the end of the last fiscal year. EVs accounted for more than 70 percent of all passenger vehicles imported into the country in the fiscal year 2023-24, and made Nepal the world’s second-largest market for EVs by share of new passenger vehicle sales, after Norway. The trend continued into 2024-25 as well.

The customs data also show that Nepal imported 227,834 unassembled motorcycles worth Rs30.35 billion and 22,820 assembled motorcycles worth Rs2.72 billion in the last fiscal year. Electric two-wheelers are also gaining ground, with imports reaching 27,183 units worth Rs2.99 billion.

articles.title: As AI-generated covers spread, Nepali musicians fight to reclaim their voices
articles.summary:
On June 29, singer Sugam Pokharel posted a status on Facebook with a stern warning. He issued an immediate demand for the removal of unauthorised AI-generated content utilising his or other artists’ works. “If you ignore this request,” he wrote, “we will have no choice but to bring you within the jurisdiction of the law, wherever you may be, in Nepal or anywhere else in the world.” The status included screenshots of AI covers of his originals uploaded on Youtube and Tiktok.

Pokharel says he first learned his songs were being run through AI months earlier, not from any platform notification but from listeners who told him directly.

He says he is not opposed to AI itself. He uses apps like Suno, the AI music creation platform, in his own creative process. He feeds in his lyrics and compositions to the app to sketch out arrangements before handing them to a producer. For an arranger, the work would take hours, if not days. Now it can be done at a fraction of the cost and time, he says.

What Pokharel objects to is the unauthorised use of his voice, melodies and lyrics. This distinction—AI as a creative tool versus a means of misappropriation—is a hot topic in Nepal’s music industry today.

The debate has reached law enforcement. Bimal Adhikari, who runs the label Bhavna Music Solution, recently took his complaint to Nepal Police’s Cyber Bureau. He first noticed songs under his label being altered and re-uploaded about six or seven months ago and initially assumed the trend would fade out on its own. It didn’t. His work was relabelled under different names and traded commercially; by the time he acted, somewhere between 40 and 50 of his songs had been altered with the help of AI, several traced to a single person operating 10 to 12 YouTube channels.

Adhikari is precise about what makes this different from AI music in general. “Even if a song is made by AI, the melody is 100 percent the melody I created,” he says. “The lyrics are also the same. It isn’t an ‘AI-generated song’. It is my composition and my words.”

Deputy Superintendent of Police Gajendra Acharya said the Bureau categorises complaints based on the nature of the offence rather than under a dedicated AI music category. As a result, it was unable to provide statistics on AI music-related complaints.

Adhikari adds he worries about what comes next. Automated copyright-detection systems, he fears, could eventually flag original artists for infringement on their own material, while the anonymous channels that triggered the confusion disappear and resurface under new names, leaving the strike behind on the real artist’s account.

Adhikari has so far filed an individual copyright complaint against around 95 YouTube channels for unauthorised use of his content. Many of the cases were later settled after those responsible apologised, acknowledged their wrongdoing and removed the offending content.

Both Pokharel and Adhikari trace part of the problem back to the law itself. Nepal’s Copyright Act was passed in 2002. Pokharel argues that it was never formulated to anticipate voice cloning. “If someone takes your house or your property, paints it a different colour, and then puts it on the market to sell, that’s illegal, isn’t it?” Pokharel says. Noting that current prime minister, Balendra Shah, is himself a musician, Pokharel says the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology should prioritise updating the laws.

Not everyone experiencing the shift sees only loss in it. Santosh Chapagain, who owns Pass Café in Kathmandu, has played AI-generated music for eight or nine months now, a habit he traces to the period around the Gen Z movement. “Music is life for musicians,” Chapagain says. “But for us, music is for entertainment, for peace of mind.” He adds, “We play whichever music makes us happy.” From devotional songs in the morning to timeless classics or rap, he plays it all in his cafe. His customers have noticed this change, some have remarked that he used to play the old songs before, but he says there has been no real pushback, and he has found uses for the technology beyond convenience: AI-generated bhajans, or turning a sad Dashain song into a happy one on request.

According to Nepal’s laws, and laws around the world, Chapagain says, using someone’s copyrighted work without permission is illegal. He would support a labelling requirement if regulators introduced one for cafés, he says. But he doesn’t see the original and the AI version as competing versions. “Original is original. Gold is still gold,” he said. “Its price changes over time, but its value remains.”

Utsaha Joshi (Uniq Poet), an artist who works with AI tools directly, says the popular image of how the music actually gets made—one prompt, one upload—is wrong. It starts with a human vision: humming a melody, writing lyrics, sometimes playing and recording instruments before any prompting begins. Only after that groundwork comes AI-assisted production, which includes prompting, re-prompting, separating stems, and assembling the result “brick by brick.” What gets automated, in this account, is manual execution, not creative direction.

If a generation draws on an artist’s own data, Joshi argues, that artist should be paid for it, however small the amount, which would require music models to be trained alongside a genuine attribution system and a clear opt-out for artists.

An AI-created cover version of Sugam Pokharel’s much-loved song “Pheri Tyo Din”.The question—how to make AI’s use of an artist’s voice visible, if not yet compensable—is what a new global labelling initiative is also attempting to address, at least on paper. Announced by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) and the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), alongside other organisations including the Grammy Awards’ organisers, the voluntary framework introduces two labels: “Created by AI,” for content where the main vocals or lead instrumental tracks were substantially AI-generated, and “AI-Assisted,” for human-made music that used AI for specific elements, with a requirement to disclose clearly if a person did not perform the main vocals or instruments.

Some platforms are already moving. Deezer now automatically tags AI-generated uploads and reports that nearly half of new submissions to the platform are AI-generated, with a detection system it says is 99.8 percent accurate. An Apple Music official said earlier this year that more than a third of new uploads to the platform are fully AI-generated. Spotify introduced a “Spotify-verified” label last April aimed at confirming official artist content and curbing AI impersonation. The Digital Media Association, which represents Apple Music, Amazon Music and Spotify, has welcomed the framework, saying it will give listeners clearer information and strengthen the metadata attached to AI content.

None of this is specific to Nepal. No domestic streaming service or regulator has proposed a comparable disclosure system, even as Nepali listeners are, by several accounts here, already encountering unlabelled AI-generated music daily: in cafés, on buses, at devotional gatherings, without being told.

Suresh Manandhar, an AI scientist, sees the same divide from a different angle. In his view, AI has genuinely lowered the barrier to making music. From cutting the cost and time of composing and writing lyrics for artists who already create, while opening music-making to people who couldn’t previously afford it. “That is a very positive effect,” he said. The problem, he said, isn’t the tool. It’s that someone who is skilled with the tool but isn’t a creator can take an original artist’s lyrics or music and “twist it into their own creation,” which is where questions of ownership and attribution—still unresolved in Nepal—begin.

Asked where the line should sit between creative use and unauthorised imitation, Manandhar reached for an analogy from his own field. “Just as we provide citations and references in academic work, any AI-generated content should be clearly labelled as ‘AI-Generated,’” he said. Voice cloning, in his view, is the clearest case for mandatory labelling and attribution. Lyrics are trickier, since reworking existing lyrics or melodies into something new predates AI, Hindi film songs have long borrowed from English or Nepali ones. He argued that the ownership rules therefore shouldn’t change just because AI was involved: if a person turns one set of lyrics into another using an AI tool, the work, and the ownership, is still theirs, and the legal question should be judged exactly as it would be without AI in the picture.

But Manandhar also cautioned that labelling alone won’t settle what Nepali musicians are asking for, because “what exactly we are protecting” is not one thing. Lyrics, musical style, audio-visual style, and an artist’s cloned voice each need their own rule, he said, rather than a single blanket policy. He offered his own hypothesis: turning a Narayan Gopal song into a rap track. That transformation was possible before AI—it would simply have taken longer by hand—so the financial and intellectual ownership of the original hit, he argued, should be treated no differently whether AI was used to do it or not.

Looking ahead, Manandhar expects the technology to move from a production shortcut to something closer to a collaborator. Within the next year, he said, artists are likely to work with AI agents that hold a working knowledge of everything they’ve previously created, letting a musician describe a mood, an instrument, or a visual setting and have the assistant draft variations to refine into a finished song—an extension, he said, of what people are already doing informally with short-form drafts on platforms like TikTok.

For now, the burden of flagging AI-generated music falls on artists themselves, checking their own catalogues, filing their own complaints, writing their own warnings on Facebook.

Adhikari says his own case is resolved, for now. But he does not think it is over. “Other friends have thousands of songs that are being used purely for trade,” he said. “I believe this issue will be raised by many others in the coming days.”

articles.title: Urgent need for market action amid skyrocketing prices
articles.summary:
The cost of daily essentials has risen again, making life more expensive for Nepali households. For instance, just three months ago, you could buy a bag of Jira Masino rice for Rs2,100, but the same strain now costs about Rs2,500. The price of leafy vegetables has skyrocketed in Kathmandu. Cooking oil and dairy products account for the largest share of people’s expenditure, while fruits, once a daily purchase for many households, have become less frequent. Commuting to and from office, schools and universities has also become costly. Kathmanduites are grappling with the artificial shortage of cooking gas in the market. As a result, families are compromising on how they eat, spend and save, with the burden falling disproportionately on low- and middle-income families.

When people complain about a pricey market, traders have their answers ready: higher import costs, an increase in the price of crude oil in the international market, seasonal supply shortages, a natural rise in demand before major festivals and rising transport expenses. These reasons are undeniable. But the Nepali market is also filled with unscrupulous traders and middlemen who artificially raise prices, leaving consumers suffering. Every year, authorities promise to keep markets under control, assuring consumers that unscrupulous traders will be held accountable and that black marketing and artificial shortages will be curtailed by deploying more market monitoring teams. Yet every year, the same story repeats, indicating that authorities are not doing enough to protect people from the excessive impact of market anomalies.

Consumer rights advocates find no solid economic reason for the ongoing rise in prices of daily essentials—and rightly so. Price hikes during tensions in West Asia were understandable, but those tensions have since eased. International supply chains are also showing signs of improvement. Even after the Department of Transport Management announced a 2 percent reduction in inter-provincial public transport fares effective from early last month, passengers are still paying the inflated price. Thanks to weak market regulation and ineffective monitoring, the public continues to bear the brunt of price hikes.

The government should not leave people to fight surging prices of daily essentials alone; it must take visible actions and come up with long-term solutions to alleviate the public woe. To begin with, it can withdraw its revenue-collecting policies such as 5 percent VAT on household electricity consumption above 50 units and 13 percent VAT on non-household use. Such policies are detrimental and will only erode trust in the government. Additionally, regular monitoring activities alone will play a big role in curbing the artificial surge in prices in the market. As the festival season approaches, the need for stronger market oversight should be dealt with urgency. Activities like spreading exaggerated predictions of food and gas shortages must be contained.

A resilient agricultural system, which is the backbone of our economy, is another essential, sustainable component for managing price hikes and reducing Nepal’s dependence on imported food and agricultural inputs. For this, investment in irrigation, storage facilities, rural roads and cold-chain infrastructure is necessary. By addressing these needs, the state can instil hope among citizens that it is committed to protecting their well-being.

articles.title: I don’t want to give my life away to Mark Zuckerberg. Do you?
articles.summary:
About a year ago, I was burned out from classes, work and life in general. For nearly a month, I ignored everyone, friends and family included. I was too deep in my own head to care. One of those days, while mindlessly scrolling Instagram, an ad stopped me cold. A woman with apparent concern in her eyes calmly said, “Not picking up calls from your loved ones, not answering texts, staying in your room all day isn’t normal, and it’s not healthy.” Of course, it ended with the usual ‘buy our product’ sales pitch. Suddenly, I started getting bombarded with similar ads.

I always thought these platforms used targeted ads based on my search history, my likes and what I watched. But I had neither googled nor had I watched reels of that kind. So why was I suddenly flooded with these ads? I felt violated. It was as if the phone’s camera was its eye; watching me silently all this time, smirking in the dark, patiently waiting for the perfect moment to throw these ads in my face. I couldn’t shake this off at all. After thinking about it for a while, I remembered all these apps I was getting calls on: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp are owned by the same corporation: Meta and at the centre of it all, Mark Zuckerberg.

Meta’s market cap is approximately $1.55 trillion, and Mark Zuckerberg’s net worth as of July is $237 billion. But the services he provides are all free. I have never paid a dollar to use any of those apps. So where does all this money come from? The answer is simple. This is just the classic case of “If you are not paying for the product, you are the product.” Meta and other tech companies are in the business of selling their users, which is you and billions of people. It sounds like ancient history now, but do you remember when entire families would gather in the living room to watch a movie or a big sports match together? During the ad breaks, we all saw the same commercials. I might have been into Nike shoes, my brother obsessed with Jordans, and my mom might be into makeup kits, yet we all had to watch the same Pepsi ad. Your TV didn’t know anything about you, and personalisation wasn’t possible.

But today, even if we’re all watching the same game or the same show, the experience is completely different. We’re each staring at our own separate screens, and those screens know us too well. I’ll get served the Nike ad, my brother will see the Jordan one, and my mom will get the makeup promotion. The ad break that once united us now divides us into perfectly targeted little bubbles. And some people might argue that this is a fair tradeoff, even a net positive. After all, the algorithm knows you better than you know yourself. It shows you exactly what you want, making it easier and faster to discover products, trends and content you think you need. While it may feel harmless on the surface, the reality is far more invasive.

Everything we do online is being tracked and measured. The algorithm knows exactly which image you stop on and how long you look at it. It knows when you’re happy, when you’re sad, when you’re secretly looking at photos of your ex, what time you go to sleep, and what time you wake up. It knows whether you’re an introvert or an extrovert, along with many other aspects of your personality. Although these are only predictions, they are becoming increasingly accurate. Shoshana Zuboff, a Harvard Business School professor and author of The Age of Surveillance Capitalism, calls this ‘behavioural futures markets’, a system where predictions about what you will do next are packaged and sold before you even do them. These platforms have collected more information about us than has ever been imagined in human history. All this data that we constantly pour out is being fed into highly automated systems, building sharper models of who we are and what we think.

I am not a customer for Meta. That would be the woman in that ad, the one trying to sell me something while I was shut off from the world. When an advertiser pays Meta to run an ad, they are not just buying exposure. They are buying certainty. Meta doesn’t just promise that your ad will be seen. It gives them certainty that the right eyes will see it, at the right moment, in the right state of mind. The woman paid Meta to reach me at the time I was most likely to buy what she was selling. That makes her the customer, me the product, and Meta the middleman that brought us together. Its entire business model is built on this. Billions of users across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp locked into an ecosystem they use every single day, the decades of accumulated behavioural data that no competitor can replicate and the ownership over the platforms and the ad auction system. Put all of that together, and the trillion-dollar valuation starts to make a lot more sense.

The User Interface (UI) is designed so the scroll feels effortless so that even at midnight, half asleep, your thumb keeps moving. There is no progress bar, no signal that time is passing. Every small decision in the interface, down to where each button is placed and how a video transitions to the next, was made by an engineer whose job was to keep you there longer. The app was not designed for your convenience. It was designed for your captivity.

Three years ago, Dino Ambrosi, a digital wellness speaker, in a TED Talk titled ‘The battle for your time’, presented a chart that mapped the life of an average 18-year-old. Assuming they’d live to 90, he calculated they’d have 864 months left. He calculated that an average person spends 288 months sleeping, 126 months at work and school, 36 months cooking, 27 months in hygiene, 36 months on chores, and 18 months driving. That leaves you with 334 months of free time. This is when you live your life. Realising that we can live only 334 out of possible 864 months of our lives, I am sure none of us wants to spend this time scrolling through social media.

According to DataReportal, the global average screen time sits at 6 hours and 40 minutes per day. That’s every single person in this world giving away more than a quarter of their day to Mark Zuckerberg for the rest of their lives. Well, count me out. I want to live, take risks, make mistakes, fail on my own terms, and find my way through life. I only got this one life, and I don’t want to give it away to Mark Zuckerberg. Do you?

articles.title: Can the Majority World keep up in the AI race?
articles.summary:
The inaugural UN Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance (UNGDAI), mandated by the UN General Assembly, took place on July 6-7 in Geneva. The United Nations General Assembly established the global dialogue as an inclusive space within the UN for governments and stakeholders to deliberate on today’s most pressing AI challenges, following intergovernmental negotiations and broad consultations with diverse stakeholders.

The four main themes of UNGDAI—AI opportunities, bridging AI divides, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, and human rights—are highly relevant to least-developed countries and regions such as Nepal. With the growing adoption of ICT, the internet and AI in recent years, there is increasing excitement in the government and the private sector about reaping the benefits of AI. Similarly, the government’s priority to regulate AI through laws and policies, including the recently adopted National AI Policy, the Data Centre and Cloud Service (Operation and Management) Directives, and its broader legislative agenda on AI, reflects the strong push by both government and businesses to capitalise on AI opportunities.

However, the discourse around bridging the digital and AI divide, ensuring AI systems are safe, secure, and trustworthy, and addressing their human rights implication remains overshadowed in Nepal. Nepal’s AI Sector Maturity score is only 0.68 out of 100 as per the Government AI Readiness Index 2025 report prepared by Oxford Insights. In such a scenario, rather than treating AI as inevitable and pushing for blind adoption, Nepal should strive to build domestic AI capabilities and infrastructure; prioritise developing a comprehensive data protection ecosystem; build resilient cybersecurity systems and practices; and conduct economic, social, cultural and environmental AI impact assessments, to ensure that the AI systems and AI governance it adopts are just, inclusive and rights-respecting.

The UNGDAI was a useful multistakeholder platform where governments, including significant participation from technology companies, civil society and academia, came together to discuss the enormous opportunities AI has already created and is expected to create in the future. There appeared to be broad agreement on the need for a global framework for AI governance. The discussions highlighted how nearly half of global investment is now directed toward AI and related sectors, and how AI is expected to transform virtually every sector, including healthcare, education, public service delivery and public governance. There seemed to be a broad consensus that AI is an ultimate game-changer.

However, questions concerning the realities of developing countries and the communities within them—those with comparatively limited stakes and agency in AI development and global AI policymaking—received less attention. Countries and communities that continue to struggle with the digital divide, and that are increasingly exposed to AI systems developed in the Minority World, in dominant languages and largely trained on data originating from those contexts, are often not even in a position to fully understand the potential repercussions of systems that may increasingly shape many aspects of their lives, including the exercise of their fundamental rights.

For many people in the Majority World, including Nepal, AI is largely understood as a tool for content generation, and ChatGPT effectively represents AI itself. In the UNGDAI, I also found limited discussion on the environmental impacts of AI ecosystems, as well as issues relating to Indigenous communities, sexual and gender minorities, and persons with disabilities. As the United Nations is the primary international institution advancing the principle of leaving no one behind, giving limited attention to these groups in AI governance discussions risks deepening their marginalisation unless greater consideration is given to designing more inclusive dialogues.

There is a pressing need to strengthen AI governance and regulatory discourse at the national and regional levels, particularly across the Majority World, where governments and other stakeholders can collectively explore their AI capacities and opportunities while working toward equitable AI development. Communities should better understand the potential impacts of AI systems on their lives and their environment. The meaningful participation of minority groups should be ensured throughout AI governance and regulatory processes. Human rights principles and standards should serve as the benchmark for AI governance and regulation.

Between now and the next round of the Dialogue in May 2027 in New York, countries from the Majority World should identify their core national and regional priorities and develop common positions on key negotiating issues. Building strategic alliances ahead of the formal negotiations will further strengthen their collective voice and bargaining power.

Equally important is strengthening the AI literacy and advocacy capacity of civil society organisations, digital rights groups, academia, and other public interest stakeholders. As these actors gain a deeper understanding of AI technologies, their societal impacts, and emerging governance challenges, they will be better positioned to advocate for AI systems that are just, ethical, trustworthy and respectful of human rights. The United Nations and development partners should therefore prioritise investing in awareness-raising, knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiatives that enable these stakeholders to meaningfully contribute to AI governance discussions and ensure that the interests and concerns of vulnerable and marginalised communities are effectively represented.
